text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation,

 $(x^{2}+1)^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}+2x(x^{2}+1)y=1$ 

such
that y(0) = 0. If $\sqrt{a}y(1)$ = $\frac{π}{32}$ , then the value of
'a' is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(x^{2}+1)^{2}\frac{dy}{dx}+2x(x^{2}+1)y=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dy}{dx}+\left (\frac{2x}{1+x^{2}}\right )y=\frac{1}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}$

I.F = $e^{\int \frac{2x}{1+x2}dx}=e^{\ln \left (1+x^{2}\right )}=1+x^{2}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{d}{dx}\left (\left (1+x^{2}\right )y\right )=\frac{1}{1+x^{2}}$

Integrating both sides we get,

$\left (1+x^{2}\right )y$ = $\tan ^{-1}x$ + C

When x = 0 then y = 0

So, 0 = 0 + C

$\Rightarrow$ C = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (1+x^{2}\right )y$ = $\tan ^{-1}x$

Put x = 1,

y.(2) = $\frac{π}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ y = $\frac{π}{8}$ = y(1)

Given,

$\sqrt{a}y(1)$ = $\frac{π}{32}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{a}.\frac{π}{8}$ = $\frac{π}{32}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{a}=\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $a=\frac{1}{16}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot

text:
If $α$ and $β$ be the roots of the equation
$x^{2} – 2x + 2 = 0$, then the least value of n for which $\left (\frac{α}{β}\right )^{n}=1$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{2} – 2x + 2 = 0$

$\therefore$ x = $\frac{2\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2}=1\pm i$

Now, $\frac{α}{β}=\frac{1+i}{1-i}=\frac{(1+i)^{2}}{1-i^{2}}=i$

or $\frac{α}{β}=\frac{1-i}{1+i}=\frac{(1-i)^{2}}{1+i^{2}}=-i$

$\therefore$ $(i)^{n}$ = 1

and $(-i)^{n}$ = 1

So n must be a multiple of 4

$\therefore$ Minimum value of n = 4
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot

text: $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\sin ^{2}x}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1+\cos x}}$ equals:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{\sin ^{2}x}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1+\cos x}}$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{\sin ^{2}x}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1+\cos x}}\right )\left (\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x}}{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x}}\right )$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{\sin ^{2}x}{1-\cos x}\right )\left (\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x}\right )$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\left (\frac{\sin ^{2}x}{2\sin ^{2}\left (\frac{x}{2}\right )}\right )\left (\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x}\right )$

= $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{\sin x}{x}\right )^{2}x^{2}\left (\frac{\frac{x}{2}}{\sin \frac{x}{2}}\right )^{2}\frac{1}{\frac{x2}{4}}\left (\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x}\right )$

= $\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 2\sqrt{2}$

= $4\sqrt{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot

text:
The mean and variance of seven observations are
8 and 16, respectively. If 5 of the observations are
2, 4, 10, 12, 14, then the product of the remaining
two observations is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given mean ($μ$) = 8

variance ($σ^{2}$) = 16

No of observations (N) = 7

Let the two unknown observation = x and y

We know,

$σ^{2}=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{N}-μ^{2}$ = 16

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2^{2}+4^{2}+10^{2}+12^{2}+14^{2}+x^{2}+y^{2}}{7}-(8)^{2}$ = 16

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2} + y^{2} = 100 ........(1)$

We know,

$μ$ = $\frac{\sum x_{i}}{N}$ = 8

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2+4+10+12+14+x+y}{7}$ = 8

$\Rightarrow$ x + y = 14 ...........(2)

As $(x + y)^{2} = x^{2} + y^{2} + 2xy$

$\Rightarrow$ $(14)^{2} = 100 + 2xy$

$\Rightarrow$ 196 = 100 + 2xy

$\Rightarrow$ xy = 48
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot

Let O(0, 0) and A(0, 1) be two fixed points. Then
the locus of a point P such that the perimeter of
$\Delta$AOP is 4, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let point C(h, k)

Given, AB + BC + AC = 4

From graph, AB = 1

$\therefore$ BC + AC = 3

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{h^{2}+k^{2}}+\sqrt{h^{2}+(k-1)^{2}}=3$

$\Rightarrow$ $h^{2}+(k-1)^{2}$ = 9 + $h^{2}+k^{2}$ - $6\sqrt{h^{2}+k^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $6\sqrt{h^{2}+k^{2}}=2k+8$

$\Rightarrow$ $9\left (h^{2}+k^{2}\right )=k^{2}+8k+16$

$\Rightarrow$ $9h^{2}+8k^{2}-8k-16=0$

$\therefore$ Locus of point C will be,

$9x^{2} + 8y^{2} – 8y = 16$

text:
The sum of the solutions of the equation 

$\left |\sqrt{x}-2\right |+\sqrt{x}\left (\sqrt{x}-4\right )+2=0$

(x > 0) is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Case 1 : When $\sqrt{x}\geq 2$

then $\left |\sqrt{x}-2\right |=\sqrt{x}-2$

$\therefore$ The given equation becomes,

$\left (\sqrt{x}-2\right )$ + $\sqrt{x}\left (\sqrt{x}-4\right )+2$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\sqrt{x}-2\right )$ + $x-4\sqrt{x}$ + 2 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $x-3\sqrt{x}$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{x}\left (\sqrt{x}-3\right )$ = 0

$\therefore$ $\sqrt{x}$ = 0 or 3

$\sqrt{x}$ = 0 is not possible as $\sqrt{x}\geq 2$.

So, $\sqrt{x}$ = 3

or $x$ = 9

Case 2 : When $\sqrt{x}<2$

then $\left |\sqrt{x}-2\right |=-\left (\sqrt{x}-2\right )$ = $2-\sqrt{x}$

$\therefore$ The given equation becomes,

$\left (2-\sqrt{x}\right )$ + $\sqrt{x}\left (\sqrt{x}-4\right )+2$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $2-\sqrt{x}$ + $x-4\sqrt{x}$ + 2 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $x-5\sqrt{x}+4$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $x-4\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{x}+4$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{x}\left (\sqrt{x}-4\right )-\left (\sqrt{x}-4\right )$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\sqrt{x}-4\right )\left (\sqrt{x}-1\right )$ = 0

$\therefore$ $\sqrt{x}$ = 4 or 1

$\sqrt{x}$ = 4 is not possible as $\sqrt{x}<2$.

$\therefore$ $\sqrt{x}$ = 1

or $x$ = 1

So, Sum of all solutions = 9 + 1 = 10
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot

text:
The area (in sq. units) of the region

A = { (x, y) $\in$ R × R|  0 $\leq$ x $\leq$ 3, 0 $\leq$ y $\leq$ 4,
 y $\leq$  $x^{2} + 3x}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


When y = 4 then,

$x^{2} + 3x = 4$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2} + 3x - 4 = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2} + 4x - x - 4 = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ x(x + 4) - (x + 4) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ (x + 4)(x - 1) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ x = 1, - 4

As 0 $\leq$ x $\leq$ 3,

so possible value of x = 1.

$\therefore$ $y = x^{2} + 3x$ parabola cut the line y = 4 at x = 1.

Required area

= $\int\limits _{0}^{1}\left (x^{2}+3x\right )dx$ + 2 $\times$ 4

= $\left [\frac{x^{3}}{3}+3\left (\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right )\right ]_{0}^{1}$ + 8

= $\left (\frac{1}{3}+\frac{3}{2}\right )$ + 8

= $\frac{11}{6}+8$ 

= $\frac{59}{6}$

text:
Let ƒ : [0, 2] $\to$ R be a twice differentiable
function such that ƒ''(x) > 0, for all x $\in$ (0, 2).
If $𝜙$(x) = ƒ(x) + ƒ(2 – x), then $𝜙$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$𝜙$(x) = ƒ(x) + ƒ(2 – x)

$\Rightarrow$ $𝜙$'(x) = ƒ'(x) - ƒ'(2 – x)

Since ƒ''(x) > 0 for all x $\in$ (0, 2)

$\Rightarrow$ ƒ'(x) is an increasing function for all x $\in$ (0, 2).

Case 1 : When $𝜙$(x) is increasing function

So $𝜙$'(x) > 0

$\Rightarrow$ ƒ'(x) - ƒ'(2 – x) > 0

$\Rightarrow$ ƒ'(x) > ƒ'(2 – x)

$\Rightarrow$ x > 2 – x

$\Rightarrow$ x > 1

 $\therefore$ $𝜙$(x) is increasing on (1, 2).

Case 2 : When $𝜙$(x) is decreasing function

So $𝜙$'(x) < 0

$\Rightarrow$ ƒ'(x) - ƒ'(2 – x) < 0

$\Rightarrow$ ƒ'(x) < ƒ'(2 – x)

$\Rightarrow$ x < 2 – x

$\Rightarrow$ x < 1

 $\therefore$ $𝜙$(x) is decreasing on (0, 1).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot

Length of perpendicular from

OM = $\left |\frac{0+0-n}{\sqrt{1^{2}+1^{2}}}\right |=\frac{n}{\sqrt{2}}$

text:
All possible numbers are formed using the digits
1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4 taken all at a time. The number
of such numbers in which the odd digits occupy
even places is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


For those three odd digit numbers 1, 1, 3 we can choose any three positions out of the four even positions.

$\therefore$ No of ways we can choose 3 positions out of the 4 positions $= ^{4}C_{3}$

After choosing those three positions, number of ways we can arrange three odd digit numbers $= ^{4}C_{3}$ $\times$ $\frac{3!}{2!}$

Then the remaining 6 digits can be arrange = $\frac{6!}{2!4!}$ ways

$\therefore$ Total number of 9 digit numbers $= ^{4}C_{3}$ $\times$ $\frac{3!}{2!}$ $\times$ $\frac{6!}{2!4!}$ = 180

If $2y=\left (\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}\cos x+\sin x}{\cos x-\sqrt{3}\sin x}\right )\right )^{2}$, 

x $\in$ $\left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$ then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$2y=\left (\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}\cos x+\sin x}{\cos x-\sqrt{3}\sin x}\right )\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2y = $\left (\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{\sqrt{3}+\tan x}{1-\sqrt{3}\tan x}\right )\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2y = $\left (\cot ^{-1}\left (\frac{\tan \frac{π}{3}+\tan x}{1-\tan \frac{π}{3}\tan x}\right )\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2y = $\left (\cot ^{-1}\tan \left (\frac{π}{3}+x\right )\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2y = $\left (\frac{π}{2}-\tan ^{-1}\tan \left (\frac{π}{3}+x\right )\right )^{2}$

As x $\in$ $\left (0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$ then

$\tan ^{-1}\tan \left (\frac{π}{3}+x\right )$ = $\left (\frac{π}{3}+x\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ 2y = $\left (\frac{π}{2}-\left (\frac{π}{3}+x\right )\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2y = $\left (\frac{π}{6}-x\right )^{2}$

$\therefore$ $2\frac{dy}{dx}=2\left (\frac{π}{6}-x\right )(-1)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dy}{dx}=\left (x-\frac{π}{6}\right )$

text:
The greatest value of c $\in$ R for which the system
of linear equations

x – cy – cz = 0

cx – y + cz = 0

cx + cy – z = 0

has a non-trivial solution, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If the system of equations has non-trivial
solutions, then

D = 0

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & -c & -c \\ c & -1 & c \\ c & c & -1 \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(1 - c^{2}) + c(-c - c^{2}) - c(c^{2} + c) = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(1 + c)(1 - c - 2c^{2}) = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(1 + c)^{2} (1 - 2c) = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ c = -1 or $\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ Greatest value of c is $\frac{1}{2}$.

text:
If cos($α$ + $β$) = 3/5 ,sin ( $α$ - $β$) = 5/13 and
0 < $α,β$ < $\frac{π}{4}$, then tan(2$α$) is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 8th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $0<α<\frac{π}{4}$

and $0<β<\frac{π}{4}$

$\therefore$ $0>-β>-\frac{π}{4}$

$\therefore$ $0<α+β<\frac{π}{2}$

and $-\frac{π}{4}<α-β<\frac{π}{4}$

As cos($α$ + $β$) = 3/5

so $\tan (α+β)=\frac{4}{3}$

As sin( $α$ - $β$) = 5/13

so $\tan (α-β)=\frac{5}{12}$

Now tan(2$α$) = tan($α$ + $β$ + $α$ - $β$)

= $\frac{\tan (α+β)+\tan (α-β)}{1-\tan (α+β)\tan (α-β)}$

= $\frac{\frac{4}{3}+\frac{5}{12}}{1-\frac{4}{3}\times \frac{5}{12}}$ = $\frac{63}{16}$
